clue.text: Large cutting tool: it's hand-held

indicators.note: held means the hand grips something, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an animal's hand is its paw
it's taken as the letters it is written with, minus the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A big saw described as something you can hold in one hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contradicts itself on purpose: a large tool is not hand-held, so the hyphenated word splits into a piece and its container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit saw is a long two-man saw once used over a sawpit to cut timber into planks.

clue.text: TV programme charts rise of star player-outside left

indicators.note: in a down light a rise reads from bottom to top, so the word for star is turned upside down

parts.note: the top performer is the star

indicators.note: outside means the player's position wraps around the letter for left

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A TV show charting a star player's rise, with a winger on the outside left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charts' is a link. Pot Black was a long-running BBC snooker programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot Black was a BBC television snooker tournament broadcast from 1969 onward.

clue.text: This comes from remote Assam

indicators.note: comes from signals the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A drink that originates in a far-flung part of India.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the end of 'remote' and the start of 'Assam', and the whole clue also defines it, since Assam is a great tea region.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam in north-east India is one of the world's biggest growing regions for the beverage leaf.

clue.text: Invite to social event daughter spurned with look of disapproval

parts.note: to invite someone is to ask them

indicators.note: spurned means the daughter is rejected, so her letter is dropped from the event

parts.note: a dance is a social event
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A daughter turned down an invitation to a party and got a disapproving look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurned' removes D from DANCE, leaving ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to regard someone with suspicion or disapproval, a sidelong glance.

clue.text: Explode, as weirdo's released?

parts.note: a weirdo is a freak, and the 's stands for is
someone released from prison is out

explanation.surface: Losing your temper, likened to an oddball let out of confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'weirdo's released' as 'the weirdo is out'; the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To freak out is slang for losing control in sudden anger or panic, a verbal blow-up.

clue.text: Part of Ascot course-really? No kidding?

indicators.note: kidding suggests the letters are being toyed with and jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone at the racecourse asks incredulously whether something is really so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kidding' rearranges COURSE, REALLY and NO. Ascot is a royal racecourse in Berkshire, England, with an exclusive area reserved for the monarch's guests.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclusive members' area at Ascot racecourse is reserved for guests invited by the monarch.

clue.text: Pacify wild animal with vegetables to eat

indicators.note: to eat means the animal takes the vegetables inside itself

parts.note: an ape is a wild animal
peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: Calming a wild beast by offering it greens to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to calm or placate them by giving way to demands.

clue.text: In a state about former wife getting summoned to court

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a row over money
an ex is a former spouse
to be cited is to be summoned to appear in court

explanation.surface: A divorcee upset because an ex-wife is being called to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up or agitated is idiomatically being in a state.

clue.text: Amplifier woman used in play

indicators.note: used in means the woman's name is placed inside the play word

parts.note: to toy with is to play with
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An actress amplified by a microphone during a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: Tannoy is a British brand name for public-address loudspeakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannoy is a trademark for loudspeaker public-address systems, used generically in Britain.

clue.text: France's top star abandoned lowly eating places

indicators.note: abandoned suggests the letters are let loose into a wild new order

parts.note: here the s of the possessive is used as a letter

explanation.surface: A leading French celebrity has given up on humble restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges FRANCES, TOP and STAR. In Britain these are roadside cafes serving lorry drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap roadside cafes catering for lorry drivers are basic places to eat in Britain.

clue.text: Tabloid's No I journalist takes year off to become a novelist

indicators.note: number one of the tabloid is its first letter, I read as the numeral one

parts.note: hack is a slang word for a journalist

indicators.note: off means the letters of year are thrown out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A tabloid's leading reporter takes a sabbatical to write a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No I' takes T from Tabloid; 'off' rearranges YEAR into ERAY. 'takes' and 'to become' are links. W. M. Thackeray wrote Vanity Fair.
explanation.definitionFit: William Makepeace Thackeray was a Victorian writer of fiction, author of Vanity Fair.

clue.text: Places regularly ignored on foot

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter of the word is skipped

explanation.surface: Spots where people stepping on foot pass without notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops the even letters L, C and S from Places, leaving PAE. 'foot' is the poetic metre unit, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A paeon is a metrical unit in verse of one long and three short syllables.

clue.text: Prohibition introduced by Trotsky, perhaps, in foreign country

indicators.note: introduced by means the prohibition is put into the name by the revolutionary

parts.note: Leon was Trotsky's first name, and perhaps marks him as one example of the name
a prohibition is a ban

explanation.surface: A Russian revolutionary bringing in a ban while abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a Middle Eastern nation on the Mediterranean, foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Bat and ball are best for playing

indicators.note: for playing suggests the letters are played around with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket remark that bat and ball are the finest kit for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for playing' rearranges BALL, ARE and BEST. 'Bat' is the flying mammal, not cricket gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The barbastelle is a European species of the flying mammal with a pug-like face.

clue.text: Plainsman completely repulsed by fiddler

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the word for completely is read backwards

parts.note: all can mean completely, as in all alone
Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A man of the prairies utterly put off by a violinist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' turns ALL into LLA; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A llanero is a cowboy of the grassy plains of Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: Coincidence, a feature of epistolary novels

definitions.meaning: agreement or matching of two things
such novels are told through letters exchanged between characters

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both matching agreement between things and the letters exchanged that form a novel told in writing.

clue.text: Unrivalled, as some holiday resorts are, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly signals the word is as spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a resort without a pier is pierless

explanation.surface: Some seaside towns are described as being without equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' asks for a word sounding like PIERLESS. British seaside resorts often have a pleasure pier running out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means having no equal, from peer in the sense of an equal.

clue.text: Decent group of performers in short entertainment in 5?

definitions.note: a cross-reference to the answer at 5-down, used here in a playful extended sense

indicators.note: in means the decent word and the troupe sit inside the shortened show
short means the entertainment loses its last letter

parts.note: ballet is a form of stage entertainment
decent can mean moral, upright
a cast is the group of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A respectable troupe putting on a short show at a racecourse enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts BALLET to BALLE. The definition stretches 5 playfully: Balmoral, the monarch's Scottish home, is an enclosed estate that is royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is a private residence of the British monarch, so its grounds are literally a regal enclosed estate.

clue.text: After short time he moves into flat, one without a rug?

indicators.note: after means the flat and its new resident follow the short time

parts.note: mo is short for moment

indicators.note: moves into means he goes inside the flat

parts.note: pad is slang for a flat or home
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shortly afterwards a man moves into an apartment without a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rug' is slang for a toupee, so someone with a thick mop of hair needs none; the surface wants a floor rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A mophead has a thick shaggy head of hair, so would never need a wig.

clue.text: Importance a Conservative attached to noble title

parts.note: count is a title of nobility

explanation.surface: Status conferred when a Tory is given an aristocratic title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attached to' is a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Account means significance or worth, as in a matter of no account.

clue.text: Famous fund-raiser, losing heart, flogged rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish suggests the remaining letters are a mess that must be rearranged
losing heart means the middle letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A celebrity fund-raiser, disheartened, sold off junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes the central G from FLOGGED, leaving FLOGED, which 'rubbish' rearranges. Bob Geldof organised Live Aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Geldof organised the Band Aid and Live Aid charity concerts raising millions for famine relief.

clue.text: European Commission, subject of discussion that's out of place

parts.note: a topic is a subject being discussed

explanation.surface: A Brussels body debating a matter that seems inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' is a medical sense: an ectopic pregnancy develops outside the womb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectopic is a medical term for something located in an abnormal position in the body.

clue.text: I'll withdraw various decrees

indicators.note: various suggests the letters are taken in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to pull out because of assorted official orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges DECREES. The definition is spoken by the answer: one who withdraws says 'I'll withdraw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seceder is one who formally breaks away from a union or church.

clue.text: English fool? The reverse: Italian sweet

indicators.note: the reverse tells us to read the English fool backwards

parts.note: a clod is a stupid person

explanation.surface: A pudding contrast: an English fool versus an Italian dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' turns ECLOD into the answer. 'fool' wants to be the English fruit pudding, but here it is a dimwit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolce is Italian for sweet, also used on menus for a dessert.

clue.text: Lucky swimmer lands in secure place close to shore

indicators.note: lands in means the swimmer ends up inside the fortified spot

parts.note: a fort is a secure stronghold
a tuna is a fish, so a swimmer

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fortunate swimmer comes ashore at a safe spot near the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the end of 'shore', taken with FORT before the swimmer goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortunate means favoured by good luck.

clue.text: Chopper, and what 'Arry does with it, say?

indicators.note: say signals the word is as pronounced, a sound-alike

parts.note: 'Arry drops his aitches, so he 'acks with a chopper rather than hacks

explanation.surface: A cockney named Harry wielding a chopping tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arry' is Harry with the H dropped, Cockney style, so his 'hacks' come out as 'acks, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe is a chopping tool with a heavy blade on a handle.

clue.text: Terrible demise after one's bitten by shark, perhaps

indicators.note: bitten by means the shark's mouth closes around the other pieces

parts.note: a shark is an example of a fish

indicators.note: after means the demise word follows the numeral

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
demise means death or end

explanation.surface: A grisly death for someone bitten by a shark.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish means extremely cruel or very difficult, as a fiend would be.

clue.text: Head removed from plump farmyard birds? Capital!

indicators.note: head removed from means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: plump means fat
hens are farmyard birds

explanation.surface: Decapitating fat chickens, then a cry of 'Excellent!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head removed from' drops F from FATHENS. 'Capital!' looks like an old exclamation of approval but is the Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.
